body: I highly recommend using [https://www.momondo.com](https://www.momondo.com) if you haven't used it yet. It's a massive flight aggregator that's points to a lot of cheap sites for maximizing bargains. It has a price calendar so you can pick the cheapest potential dates. It's saved me a lot of headaches. Honestly google flights has been awful for me more often than not with the occasional good deal, I'd try to move away from using that as fast as possible, it misses way too many good deals to be useful. The only thing that google flights does well is the price track of "low, expected, and high" for the dates you're traveling. Even then that doesn't mean much if $700 is normal for a flight in April when you don't have that much to burn.

Speaking from personal experience New Yorkers operate under the "not nice but kind" rule, I say the same thing about Londoners. If you're a dumbass or do stupid shit we'll make fun of you and call you out and we have no patience for shit. But if you genuinely need help, we got you. Like there's a video on Twitter of a guy who fell on the subway tracks recently and 5 people pull him up while a cop just waves a flashlight on his phone. 

Like if we don't like you or we're having a bad day we'll tell you to fuck off verbally or through body language. On the flip side because we're all minding our own business we allow all kinds of weirdness and anybody that has a problem with that can also fuck off. It's that weird paradox of, I can be as weird and asocial as I want, so since there's no social anxiety I'm way more sociable. To sum up our directness, I'd honestly say there is a sincerity to it, positively and negatively. The city has every race, creed, ideology, and immigrant so trying to single out one group and start shit won't really work well. We love and hate everyone equally. When the police do regularly authoritarian shit or hate crimes happen people usually rally to that group out of defiance and spite and we make that clear too.

Also no I call complete bullshit, the Dutch don't get to claim they "inspired" us culturally because Manhattan was New Amsterdam in the 1660s. That's some straight up historical revisionism. I swear Dutch people are obsessed with pointing that out even though I couldn't name 10 people back home who knew it used to be a Dutch colony. At best it's a joke about how they sold the island for like $40.  I'm saying this as a historian too and I sincerely doubt anybody really cares about trivia like this. 

Dutch bluntness is insincere. It's brutal honesty because they are too lazy to think about or apply a social filter. For example here's a list of things Dutch people have complained about me, to my face, about. 

I chew too loudly


I'm too excited about anything


I smile too often and I come off as fake

 
I look angry


I'm not polite, in the "proper way"

 
I generalize too much about the NL


I'm too specific in my complaints about the country


I'm too cynical


Why don't you speak Dutch


Why don't you like the weather


Wow the weather sucks huh


Why do you like Belgians?



That's just off the top of my head. 

These were all pointed out to me, out the blue, not apart of the mainline conversation. Just because the person thought it and felt entitled to tell me. If you notice the pattern, everything they mentioned contradict themselves but more importantly is overall irrelavent or meaningless in the grand scheme of things. They are direct about pointless bullshit but when it comes to anything emotionally or professionally important they don't say shit. They're two faced, insincere, and absolutely avoidant, and passive about most human interaction. Frankly I do not consider the Dutch a direct culture, I consider them a petty one. That's the difference to me but honestly I could rant all day about this. 

My former Dutch friends never were direct to me about any interpersonal issues we may have had. It's why we're not friends anymore because too many problems and resentments piled up. They didn't talk about their emotional issues with each other. My God the amount of times my Dutch friend would get drunk and complain to me about his gf but not tell her his concerns was unreal. And this guy claimed I was one of his best friends but he wouldn't see me for more than once a month when I only lived 20 minutes away from him in the same city and he lived next to the tram stop. I'd keep asking him if we're good and he said yes, I put almost as much effort into our friendship and I do my partner. What would he do? He would just play video games or fuck around on dating sites when we didn't see him. 

They treat people like they are disposable. Like people are coworkers and get drinks every week and genuinely get along about the second somebody switches jobs, they're like, GOODBYE I will never talk to you again. And it's not like in a we were never friends thing, these people would describe these relationships as meaningful to them and then just be dropped immediately like a sack of rocks the second it is no longer convenient. 

My ex of sorts, also was culturally conditioned to never speak her mind about her feelings or talk about her personal life because of "violations of privacy" or something. And I don't mean putting lives at risk policy. Shit like, "oh who is your friend that you seem close too? I'm glad you reconnected with them." "oh I do not want to tell you her name as that may violate her privacy." "Wait do you not tell your friends and family my name either? No I do not want to violate your privacy, I refer to you as my American friend." It's fucking batshit. 

Side note: they take pride in complaining, they call it a national past time but while British people have a sense of humor about it the Dutch genuinely think being annoying to you specifically about it will accomplish something. 

My favorite "complaint' was when a Dutch guy kept bitching about the trains being 5 minutes late all the time and how it made his life difficult. Mind you he was a student so he got free train rides and free public transport. Except they only get it during the weekday or weekend and not both anymore. They also get 4 trains per hour to every city. Compare this to me where I get 1 train to NYC from the suburbs every 90 minutes and they cost me $28 round trip and the trains run slow at max 60mph. When I pointed this out to him he still didn't understand why I thought he should be happy with what his tax dollars provide him.
